title: Optional responsibility fields on every asset type
steps: Create a business, server, service and domain with existing required fields only. Save, close and reopen each editor.
expected: No new field is required. Blank contact means Not recorded; existing fields and asset identity survive.
automation: rust-tests: asset_context::tests (partial); manually repeat all four empty forms

title: Persist full responsibility context
steps: For all four asset types set Alex, Casey, Production, Link available, https://example.com/runbook and Ticket TEST-100. Save and restart the isolated application.
expected: Each asset retains its own contacts, environment, documentation state/link and source. Server uses one environment field.
automation: rust-tests: asset_context::tests; manual native restart and all-four field comparison

title: Explicit unknown and not-applicable states
steps: Enter Unknown and Not applicable as contacts. Cycle documentation through Not recorded, Unknown, Not applicable and Link available; save and reopen each state.
expected: States remain distinct; inactive documentation states do not retain an actionable stale link.
automation: rust-tests: documentation_states_and_links_are_explicit (partial); manual full state cycle

title: Documentation validation and atomic save
steps: In an isolated new-server form enter a non-HTTP documentation path or an incomplete HTTPS address; save. Correct it to https://example.com/runbook and save once.
expected: Invalid save shows an actionable error and creates neither server nor SSH service. Correct save creates exactly one server and linked pending SSH service.
automation: rust-tests: documentation_states_and_links_are_explicit; invalid_context_rolls_back_server_and_automatic_ssh

title: Open documentation only by explicit action
steps: Edit and save an HTTPS documentation reference. Move between tabs, select the row and reopen its editor. Finally click Open reference.
expected: Editing and selection do not open a browser. Explicit Open reference opens the saved URL once.
automation: Not automated: native browser integration

title: Draft isolation and cancel behavior
steps: Edit an existing service contact without saving, close the editor, reopen the draft and then start a new service. Repeat for domain, server and business.
expected: Document current draft-retention behavior; unsaved content never changes persisted rows or leaks into a new or different asset draft.
automation: rust-tests: inventory_ui_loads_context_and_new_draft_does_not_leak_contacts (service/domain partial); manual other editors

title: Readable punctuation and long ordinary content
steps: Use names with apostrophes, accents, ampersands and 200-character notes; save and search their distinctive tokens at the largest font.
expected: Text round-trips without truncating stored values, breaking the editor or making Save unreachable; visible truncation has a way to inspect full content.
automation: Not automated: content and native layout inspection

title: Manual check and reviewer persistence
steps: For all four asset types mark I checked this information with reviewer Alex; save and reopen. Repeat with an empty reviewer.
expected: Check time persists; optional reviewer may be empty. Check is described as local manual evidence, not recipient acceptance.
automation: rust-tests: business_context_survives_noop_hide_and_expires_after_edit; invalid_context_rolls_back_server_and_automatic_ssh; service_and_domain_context_checks_are_consistent (reviewer-empty manual)

title: No-op save preserves the original check
steps: Check each asset, record its check time, save twice without changing values and restart.
expected: Original check time and reviewer remain unchanged; saving alone does not extend validity.
automation: rust-tests: business_context_survives_noop_hide_and_expires_after_edit; invalid_context_rolls_back_server_and_automatic_ssh; service_and_domain_context_checks_are_consistent

title: Changed information invalidates check
steps: On checked assets independently change contact, source, name, notes, environment and service/domain hosting. Recheck before each edit. Also edit a server cell.
expected: Relevant edits clear obsolete check status in both detail and list views; another asset is unaffected.
automation: rust-tests: service_and_domain_context_checks_are_consistent; business_context_survives_noop_hide_and_expires_after_edit; invalid_context_rolls_back_server_and_automatic_ssh (partial field matrix)

title: Ninety-day review boundary
steps: Use disposable fixture copies with check ages 89, 90 and 91 days, keeping the application clock unchanged. Compare displayed due state and exported timestamp to the rule in asset_context.rs.
expected: The implemented 90-day boundary is consistent across asset types; expired evidence is visibly due and not silently renewed. Record exact UTC timestamps and boundary semantics.
automation: rust-tests: migration_preserves_existing_checks_and_review_deadline covers 91 days only; 89/90-day boundaries require fixture acceptance

title: Hide and restore preserve context
steps: Check an asset, hide it, inspect Hidden, restore it and restart. Repeat for all four types.
expected: Context and original check are retained; hidden assets are excluded from ordinary lists unless requested.
automation: rust-tests: business_context_survives_noop_hide_and_expires_after_edit plus storage visibility tests (partial); manual all-four context cycle

title: Permanent deletion does not orphan context
steps: In a disposable fixture only, permanently delete assets where supported; reopen and verify related context and relationship rows using a read-only DB inspection.
expected: No orphan context remains and unrelated resources are preserved; unsupported delete actions are recorded as not applicable with evidence.
automation: rust-tests: business_context_survives_noop_hide_and_expires_after_edit covers business deletion; other asset types manual

title: Clean startup and reopen
steps: Start with a new isolated data directory; create a fixture, quit normally and restart twice.
expected: Schema 21 opens, saved records persist and no duplicate seed, server or SSH rows appear.
automation: rust-tests: migrates_and_seeds_an_empty_database; file_database_survives_reopen_without_duplicate_seed

title: Real schema-20 fixture migration
steps: Create a disposable schema-20 workspace with the matching older binary containing all asset types, links, hidden rows and checked entries. Copy it; open the copy with the new binary, then reopen.
expected: Counts, IDs, links, existing fields and check history survive. New context defaults correctly. backups/pre-schema-21.db exists and can be opened with the older binary.
automation: rust-tests: migration_preserves_existing_checks_and_review_deadline and file_migration_backup_restore_and_context_filtered_export are partial/replay coverage; genuine old-binary fixture remains manual

title: Migration rollback and newer-schema rejection
steps: Run existing repository migration rollback and newer-schema rejection tests. On fixture copies verify an older binary refuses the schema-21 file without modifying it.
expected: Rejected migration preserves original schema/data; old binary never silently downgrades a newer workspace.
automation: rust-tests: rejects_unknown_newer_schema; failed_inventory_migration_rolls_back_schema_and_preserves_servers (older migration coverage); manual schema-21 old-binary check

title: Complete SQLite backup and restore
steps: Create all four assets with contacts, checks, tags, hidden rows and relationships. Back up; edit/delete fixture records; restore the backup, restart and compare the complete snapshot.
expected: Full workspace including responsibility context and relationship identities is recovered; no partial JSON/CSV exchange is represented as full backup.
automation: rust-tests: database_backup_restores_previous_state; inventory_migration_backup_restore_and_reopen_preserve_links; file_migration_backup_restore_and_context_filtered_export (partial combined fixture)

title: Recovery with older snapshot and binary
steps: Preserve the schema-21 fixture separately. Launch the matching older binary with a copy of pre-schema-21.db in a separate directory; return to the new binary and preserved schema-21 fixture.
expected: Both workspaces open with their matching versions. New edits are retained in the preserved new database; rollback does not promise to backport them.
automation: Not automated: binary-pair recovery rehearsal

title: Invalid exchange or cancelled file operation preserves workspace
steps: Use ordinary invalid JSON and a non-backup text file in the isolated workspace. Attempt import/restore, then cancel an export picker. Compare counts and contacts before and after.
expected: Clear validation or cancellation; no existing record or backup is overwritten on failed operations.
automation: rust-tests: invalid_json_import_preserves_existing_workspace (partial); manual file dialogs and restore rejection

title: Search by responsibility and references
steps: Across all four views search unique tokens from technical contact, backup, source and documentation URL; clear search and combine with an existing filter.
expected: Matching assets appear, unrelated ones do not; clearing restores the view, and combined filter semantics match the controls.
automation: rust-tests: file_migration_backup_restore_and_context_filtered_export covers filtered service export only; manual four-view search matrix

title: Tags, hidden state and filter scope
steps: Create tagged active and hidden assets with the same contact. Apply a tag and contact search, switch tabs, toggle Hidden and clear filters.
expected: No hidden data appears unexpectedly; tag/search combination and per-view persistence are understandable and stable.
automation: Not automated: combined per-view UX

title: Filtered service and domain CSV includes context
steps: Export services and domains after contact search, tag and visibility filtering. Inspect headers and exact rows in a text editor before opening a spreadsheet.
expected: Only selected scope is exported with contact, backup, environment, documentation state/link, source and check metadata; no unrelated hidden row leaks.
automation: rust-tests: file_migration_backup_restore_and_context_filtered_export covers service contact/export subset; manual domain/filter matrix

title: Spreadsheet text and quoting remain literal
steps: Use fictional contact/notes starting with =1+1, +1, -1 or @text plus comma, quote and newline. Export service/domain CSV and inspect raw quoting, then open it in a spreadsheet.
expected: Formula-looking text stays text; delimiters, quotes and line breaks preserve cell boundaries and values.
automation: rust-tests: existing inventory CSV tests (partial); manual spreadsheet confirmation

title: Partial exchange formats have explicit limits
steps: Export server CSV and legacy project JSON, then inspect which fields are present. Compare their labels/help with full SQLite backup.
expected: Partial formats do not claim recovery of all context or full workspace. Record any missing UI explanation as an issue.
automation: Not automated: product copy and format limitations

title: Automatic pending SSH and independent service ports
steps: Add a server, inspect its single pending SSH service on port 22. Add MySQL on 3306 and PostgreSQL on 5432 linked to the same server; confirm each separately and edit a service port.
expected: Exactly one default SSH row; each service retains its port, protocol, notes and server link. Servers do not mix service ports into an ambiguous cell.
automation: rust-tests: server_services_are_pending_linked_and_created_atomically; invalid_context_rolls_back_server_and_automatic_ssh; manual service edit workflow

title: Business-domain-server-service graph direction
steps: Create business Commerce, domain example.com, server Origin and service API; link them. Select the business in Connections, then inspect dependencies and change hosting through the normal form.
expected: Business scope includes the actual server; domain to server to service remains visible without skipping the host. Edits update the graph and stored links.
automation: rust-tests: existing topology and relationships tests (partial); manual selected-business graph inspection

title: Details and activity records are understandable
steps: Open linked host details from a service, inspect core notes and timestamps; edit, hide and restore a fixture host and reopen details.
expected: Host identity and core context are clear. Available activity records are accurate; absent historical events are reported rather than invented.
automation: Not automated: detail and activity UI review

title: Fictional credential hide, reveal and copy
steps: Use a made-up credential only. Save, hide/reveal, copy and restart; check captured logs and screenshots before retaining them.
expected: Default masking and explicit actions work. No real credential is used, and fixture secret values are excluded from retained reports. Record platform-specific encryption/portability behavior.
automation: Not automated: native clipboard and platform credential integration

title: Import mapping and duplicate policies
steps: Import a small fictional server CSV with custom columns using skip/update duplicate policies. Inspect linked SSH rows, then repeat the import.
expected: Stable identity, custom fields and policies survive; no accidental duplicate default service is introduced.
automation: rust-tests: imports_mapped_rows_and_custom_columns_atomically; import_duplicate_policy_skips_and_updates_by_stable_keys; manual SSH import interaction

title: All five font sizes and two themes
steps: On Businesses, Servers, Services, Domains, Connections and Settings select all five font stops in light and dark themes, including open editors; restart at the largest font.
expected: Content scales consistently; settings persist, controls remain distinguishable, no overlapping text or unreachable action. Slider labels communicate the chosen scale.
automation: ui-static; rust-tests: narrow_largest_font_editor_gives_the_form_room_and_keeps_save_reachable and existing layout tests (partial); manual 60-state matrix

title: Narrow and wide editor layout
steps: At maximum font inspect 1100x720 and 1440x900 physical windows. Scroll business/server forms; open service/domain editors, close and reopen them. Inspect widths immediately around the implemented breakpoint.
expected: Narrow service/domain form uses available width; Save/Close remain reachable. Wide layout has legible table and editor. Business action footer is reachable without occluding fields.
automation: rust-tests: narrow_largest_font_editor_gives_the_form_room_and_keeps_save_reachable; manual native physical-window captures

title: Table fit, header and per-tab preferences
steps: Populate long names and short ports; choose Fit columns on Servers only. Scroll vertically and horizontally, resize and switch tabs.
expected: Header stays identifiable; columns use space sensibly, right-side actions remain reachable, and unrelated tab preferences do not change.
automation: rust-tests: table_fit_preferences_are_independent_and_preserve_legacy_choices; manual scrolling/layout

title: Modal focus and keyboard-only paths
steps: Use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Escape to create/save/cancel an asset and open Guide/details. While a modal is open try to reach the underlying tab strip with keyboard and pointer.
expected: Visible logical focus, no accidental save or focus behind a modal; closing returns focus to a useful origin. Background navigation is blocked where the window is modal.
automation: Not automated: complete native keyboard/modal acceptance

title: Screen reader and button clarity
steps: Use Narrator or NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS for contact entry, documentation state, checked status and Save. Inspect light/dark button, field and disabled states.
expected: Controls announce meaningful names/states; buttons are distinguishable from inputs without relying only on color; no spurious underlines or invisible focus.
automation: Not automated: assistive technology acceptance; ui-static provides only partial contrast evidence

title: Actual DPI and multiple displays
steps: Repeat the largest-font asset save at real OS scale 125%, 150% and 200%, move between different-DPI displays and reconnect a display.
expected: No inaccessible dialog, clipped primary action or misplaced pointer hit area. Record physical size, OS scale and renderer with screenshots.
automation: Not automated: native OS/display matrix

title: Representative inventory and interaction timings
steps: Prepare isolated 100, 1000 and 10000 asset fixtures. Warm once, measure 20 search/filter operations and 20 graph drags on each; record hardware, dataset, p50/p95 elapsed time, CPU and memory.
expected: Proposed acceptance: at 1000 assets search-to-painted-result p95 <=300ms, drag frame p95 <=33ms on agreed baseline hardware. At 10000 record limits and no sustained freeze; assess against an agreed budget before pass.
automation: Not automated: native paint/frame profiling; prior 94.6191ms single model-refresh observation is not this measurement

title: Long-session stability
steps: For 60 minutes cycle tabs, searches, editors, theme/font changes and graph drags using a 1000-asset fixture; sample memory every five minutes and restart to compare saved counts.
expected: No repeated memory growth without a plateau, lost changes or unusable UI. Establish an agreed memory budget before declaring numerical performance pass.
automation: Not automated: native session observation

title: Windows install, upgrade and preserved workspace
steps: In a disposable Windows user profile install the previous signed/released installer, create fixture data, then upgrade using the candidate installer. Launch, check app version, compare data and uninstall after preserving a backup.
expected: Correct installed version; no duplicate app or lost data. Uninstall behavior matches the stated data-retention policy. Record OS prompts and installer hash.
automation: release-build compiles only; installer lifecycle is manual

title: Linux packages on local build host
steps: Build Linux packages on the authorized local host/192.168.1.7; install candidate DEB and AppImage in disposable supported environments and repeat first-run, upgrade, backup and restore.
expected: Packages launch with runtime dependencies available; data and relationships survive upgrade. Record distro, architecture, desktop/session and package hashes.
automation: Existing package-linux scripts prepare artifacts; full package acceptance not automated by run-test-plan.py

title: Both macOS architectures
steps: For an authorized release obtain Intel and Apple Silicon DMGs from the designated GitHub builds. Mount, install, launch and upgrade on matching Macs; exercise context save, backup and native links.
expected: Both versions exist and run on matching architecture; version/hash, signing and OS prompts are documented. No claim based on cross-compilation alone.
automation: Not automated: macOS hardware and DMG lifecycle; no GitHub job is triggered by this test runner

title: Homepage and demo reflect current product
steps: Run the website suite against the candidate local files. Inspect IT in a glance messaging, current screenshots, demo businesses and graph in desktop/mobile widths.
expected: Screenshots and demo match implemented features; no unimplemented handover acceptance promise. Layout remains readable at 390x844, 768x1024 and 1440x900.
automation: website optional gate: existing Playwright suite (partial); manual copy/screenshot comparison

title: Download buttons and checksum agreement
steps: Inspect every platform/version button, including both DMGs. After an authorized candidate deployment fetch each linked artifact and sha256sums from itgla.com, hash the downloaded file and compare.
expected: All advertised links resolve, platform buttons are consistent, version and hashes match. Missing binaries or checksum manifests block release.
automation: website optional gate: existing local route tests (partial); deployed artifacts/hash check remains manual and read-only

title: Sitemap and LLM content agree with canonical pages
steps: Compare local sitemap.xml, llms.txt and any advertised llm.txt URL with canonical site routes, version/platform claims and footer links. After authorized deployment repeat read-only on itgla.com.
expected: Canonical URLs agree; no stale version, missing referenced page or contradictory feature claim. Do not require an unadvertised alias solely by filename convention.
automation: english and website footer/Playwright checks (partial); semantic consistency review manual

title: Cookies layout and site accessibility
steps: Inspect cookies and other legal pages at three website widths with 200% browser zoom, keyboard navigation and light/dark system preference.
expected: Consistent content width/alignment, reachable links and no clipped text. Native app font controls are not confused with browser zoom.
automation: website optional gate: existing Playwright site tests (partial); manual zoom and accessibility

title: Download analytics totals explain unknown country
steps: Use only the local synthetic analytics fixture to compare daily total, known-country sums and unknown/unclassified counts. Exercise date boundaries and zero-count countries through supported fixture data.
expected: Aggregate definitions reconcile; unknown locations are explicit, with no invented real download records or live analytics writes.
automation: Not automated by this runner: local fixture acceptance only

title: Thirty-second asset lookup
steps: Give five representative IT operators/developers the same fictional business. Without coaching ask who owns API, which server hosts it, what port it uses, where the runbook is and whether information needs review. Time from request to correct answer.
expected: Proposed target: at least 4/5 complete the lookup within 30 seconds without a critical wrong answer. Record actual times and confusing terms, not an assumed pass.
automation: Not automated: real-user product acceptance

title: Ten-minute inventory setup
steps: Ask the same five participants to create one business, two servers, three services and a domain with contacts, source and documentation; confirm pending SSH entries and locate an outdated record.
expected: Proposed target: at least 4/5 finish within ten minutes without assistance or lost data; collect blockers and terminology feedback.
automation: Not automated: real-user onboarding study
